title: Workload Identity
tagline: Services call each other all day with no person in the loop. How does one know who is calling, and what that caller may do?

client.name: Caller
client.brief: A service that needs something from another. Has to prove what it is.

application.name: Mesh Proxy
application.brief: Sits between services and enforces which may talk to which.

idp.name: Issuer
idp.brief: Checks what a workload really is, then gives it a short-lived identity.

mcp.name: Service
mcp.brief: The one being called. Decides whether to answer, and with what.

teaches: A workload's identity comes from what it is (attested), not from where it runs or what it says its name is.
Identities are short-lived and stay inside the workload. A stolen one soon stops working.
Knowing who is calling is half of it. What that caller may do is a separate question.

glossary.means: A cryptographic name for a running service, issued after checking what it actually is.
Evidence about a workload (its image, its node, its service account) that the issuer checks before issuing.
Both ends of a connection present a certificate, so each knows who the other is.
The set of identities issued by one authority. Another organisation's is trusted only if you chose to federate with it.
Being inside the network earns nothing. Every call is authenticated and authorised.
Withdrawing an identity before it expires, because its key may be in the wrong hands.
